Title: Experts: Cut off market for stolen cables to cripple syndicates
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Shutting down the market for stolen cables by zeroing in on unscrupulous scrapyard operators could cripple cable theft syndicates disrupting critical infrastructure nationwide.
Describing cable theft as economic sabotage, senior lawyer Kitson Foong said enforcement must go beyond arresting cable thieves and target scrap metal dealers who knowingly buy stolen cables.
"Every stolen metre of cable has a buyer. Shut the scrapyard door and the thief has nowhere to sell," he told the New Straits Times.
The copper conductor running inside the cable is much sought after. In Malaysia, copper is priced at between RM56 and RM60 per kilogramme.
Foong said Malaysia has enough laws, but the weakness lay in how offenders were charged and sentenced.
Police investigate cable theft cases under Section 431A of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum two years's jail for mischief involving damage to cables.
He said that was hardly a deterrent for syndicates earning up to RM100,000 per operation.
"Syndicates making up to RM100,000 a job are likely to walk away with three or four months' jail time. At that point, it's not a crime anymore, it's looking more like a business model!"
[[nid:1554884]]
Foong said prosecutors should bring heavier charges where evidence supported them, including theft under Section 379 of the Penal Code, which carries up to seven years' jail.
Section 235 of the Communications and Multimedia Act provides penalties of up to RM500,000 or five years' jail for offences involving telecommunications infrastructure.
Section 37 of the Electricity Supply Act 1990 provides up to RM1 million in fines or 10 years' imprisonment for dangerous interference with electrical installations.
Repeat offenders could face enhanced punishment under Section 75, while Section 411 of the Penal Code, which deals with dishonestly receiving stolen property, carried up to five years' jail.
"This should be used much more against scrap dealers, and those caught should lose their licence under the Second-hand Dealers Act," he said.
Foong proposed a specific offence for interference with critical infrastructure, carrying mandatory imprisonment and forfeiture of vehicles and criminal proceeds.
He said Section 124K of the Penal Code, on sabotage, could be applied in appropriate cases, but warned against overuse.
"It's a scalpel, not a sledgehammer. Law enforcement should aim it at organised syndicates, not some desperate guy with a hacksaw.
"A cable thief isn't just stealing copper, he's stealing a train's ability to signal safely!
"We're charging saboteurs as if they were pilferers, and that really has to stop."
Senior criminologist Datuk Dr P. Sundramoorthy said enforcement agencies must investigate the entire criminal supply chain, not just those caught stealing.
"Where middlemen or unscrupulous scrap-metal businesses knowingly buy stolen cables, they can help sustain demand and make repeated offending commercially attractive."
Investigations should target organisers, transporters, financiers, middlemen and buyers, while scrap dealers should face tighter safeguards, including seller identification, transaction records and risk-based inspections.
But Sundramoorthy cautioned against assuming that every cable theft involved a syndicate or that all dealers were complicit.
"Disrupting the market for stolen cables may be as important as arresting the people who steal them.
"If stolen material becomes difficult to sell, the financial incentive for offending is reduced."
Sundramoorthy said cable theft should be treated economic sabotage and a serious infrastructure-security problem because its consequences far exceed the value of stolen materials.
"When railway signalling or power cables are cut, train services can be disrupted, passengers may be stranded, and safety systems may be compromised."
He pointed to figures disclosed in Parliament in July showing 393 cable theft incidents involving railway assets since 2024, with estimated losses of RM16.3 million — in railway assets alone.
Sundramoorthy said copper's high resale value, coupled with weak surveillance and accessible locations make cable theft attractive.
He backed plans to review railway-related laws, including raising fines for cable theft and trespassing from RM1,000 to as much as RM100,000 per offence.
But harsher penalties alone would not deter offenders who reckon they will not be caught.
"Deterrence depends not only on the severity of punishment but also on the likelihood of detection, arrest and successful prosecution."
He said punishment should reflect the wider harm — repair costs, service disruptions and risks to public safety — not merely the resale value of stolen cables.
He supported specific aggravated offences for critical infrastructure theft, provided the laws clearly defined offences and ensured proportionate punishment.
Sundramoorthy also called for stronger intelligence-sharing between police, infrastructure operators and regulators, alongside improved CCTV surveillance, access controls and financial investigations.
"Ultimately, harsher punishments alone will not solve cable theft."

Title: Cable thieves emerge from the shadows
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Once content with operating under cover of darkness, cable thieves are becoming increasingly brazen, stripping valuable copper from the nation's infrastructure in broad daylight — sometimes in full view of passing motorists and residents. What was once associated with secluded railway tracks and poorly guarded infrastructure has evolved into organised operations targeting telecommunications networks, electricity installations and other public utilities.
The growing audacity was laid bare last Friday when four masked men used vehicles to pull out underground cables in Kampung Melayu Panchor, Seremban, around noon. The incident, captured on video, led to the arrest of 14 people, including two women.
Beyond the brazen nature of the thefts lies a much larger concern: the systematic targeting of critical infrastructure amounts to economic sabotage. While thieves may walk away with copper worth thousands of ringgit, operators face millions in repair costs, service interruptions and damaged equipment.
Seremban police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Yatim Osman said the suspects, aged 22 to 67, were detained in Labu and Nilai in Negri Sembilan and Dengkil in Selangor. Police also seized five cars, cable-cutting equipment and three sacks of burnt copper wires.
Investigators believe the arrests solved several cable theft cases in Negri Sembilan, Selangor, Kedah and Melaka.
The burnt copper wires highlighted an important aspect of the illicit trade — processing before sale. Syndicates strip insulation and remove identifying markings before selling to scrap metal dealers, making it difficult to trace the metal once it enters the recycling supply chain.
This is what makes it difficult for law enforcement to take stern action against scrap metal dealers. Without a confession, it would be difficult to tie them to stolen cables.
The financial incentive is substantial. Copper prices in Malaysia vary by purity, grade and market conditions. Clean, stripped copper commands considerably more than insulated cables or mixed metal scrap.
Demand is driven by expanding networks, renewable energy installations, data centres and the electric vehicle (EV) industry. Data centres require extensive cabling and transformers, while EVs generally use substantially more copper than petrol vehicles.
In Malaysia copper is priced at RM56 to RM60 per kilogramme.
Prasarana Malaysia Bhd previously revealed that syndicates used hollow sections of elevated Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) viaducts as temporary hideouts.
Its group chief health, safety, security, environment and sustainable development officer Idzqandar Abu Bakar said some intruders hid inside the structures for two or three days.
"They come out at certain times to climb onto the tracks to cut cables," he said.
Cable theft incidents increased from 42 cases in 2024 to 72 last year.
Idzqandar said the criminals had become more sophisticated, moving beyond earthing cables to target live electrical and signalling cables.
He said syndicates could make between RM50,000 and RM100,000 from stolen components in a single night.
Railway infrastructure is no longer the only major target. Telecommunications cables buried beneath roads and in residential areas, as well as electricity infrastructure, have increasingly attracted syndicates.
Several cable thefts involving MRT, KLIA Ekspres and KLIA Transit services have forced temporary service adjustments.
The persistence of such crimes despite repeated arrests has raised questions over whether current enforcement and penalties are sufficient.
Kuala Lumpur police recorded 205 cable theft cases last year, resulting in 171 arrests, while another 71 cases and 85 arrests were recorded between January and May.
With syndicates increasingly prepared to operate in broad daylight, tackling the problem may require authorities to look beyond those caught physically cutting cables. The wider criminal supply chain — organisers, processors and buyers of copper of questionable origin — remains crucial.
Unless the market for stolen copper is disrupted, cable theft risks remaining a lucrative criminal enterprise.
The New Straits Times has contacted Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk M. Kumar and is awaiting his response.

Title: US fines Bank of America US$1.2 billion for anti-money laundering violations
Article:
WASHINGTON: The US Treasury Department said on Tuesday that it was imposing penalties of more than US$1.2 billion on Bank of America, citing "violations of anti-money laundering and sanctions laws".
The second-biggest US bank failed to properly report more than US$5 billion in "suspicious transactions", the department said.
Some of these involved national security risks and other concerns, including transactions "indicative of Chinese money laundering networks" and illicit finance around the southwest US border.
The overall charge involves US$1.2 billion assessed by the Treasury Department's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network. This includes a US$750 million civil penalty from a key bank regulator, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC).
The Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control also announced an US$11.6 million settlement with the bank over "apparent violations of numerous sanctions programmes, including on Iran, Russia, narcotics, and global terrorism".
"Today's actions send a clear message that even the biggest financial institutions are not above the law," US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in a statement.
"When a bank of this size fails to meet its anti-money laundering and sanctions obligations, the consequences extend far beyond its own walls, exposing the entire US financial system to significant illicit finance risks," he said.
The announcement marks a blow to Bank of America just a day before it reports its third-quarter earnings.
A Bank of America spokesperson told AFP its results would include a US$1.2 billion charge, reducing net income by around 17 cents per share.
The spokesperson added that the institution was committed to completing the work needed to address issues raised by regulators.
"We will continue to support federal and local law enforcement across thousands of investigations and report hundreds of thousands of suspicious activity reports each year," the spokesperson said.
US regulators have published a consent order requiring Bank of America to work with a third party to identify and report suspicious transactions that went undetected.
The institution will also have to undergo an independent review of its programmes for monitoring suspicious activity and other forms of due diligence.
The bank is also subject to a December 2024 cease-and-desist order calling for it to address issues in its anti-money laundering programme and compliance with the Bank Secrecy Act.
However, the Treasury noted on Tuesday that the bank "failed to prioritise" compliance despite agreeing to the 2024 order.
Due to Bank of America's "egregious and continued" violations of the Bank Secrecy Act, the OCC imposed its largest civil money penalty against a bank, Comptroller of the Currency Jonathan Gould said.
Bank of America shares were down 2.6 per cent in after-hours trading following the Treasury's announcement.

Title: Anwar condemns international community’s failure to end Palestinian suffering
Article:
BANGI, Oct 14 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has condemned the failure of the international order to address the suffering of the Palestinian people.
He said the international community should remain steadfast in upholding the principles of democracy and human rights, but its response to the plight of the Palestinians exposed contradictions in its commitment to fighting colonialism and imperialism.
“What is so hypocritical is the failure of the international community. I have to speak as prime minister, I understand that. But I have to express my utter disgust with the failure of the international order.
“We talk of democracy, whose democracy? We talk of human rights, which human? When human beings are treated as animals and slaves,” he said in his speech at the Sumud Nusantara Dinner, held in conjunction with the Global Sumud Congress 2026, here yesterday.
Anwar, who is also the Patron of Sumud Nusantara, also questioned whether the different treatment accorded to the Palestinian issue was influenced by the fact that Palestinians were Arabs or Muslims.
“To me, it does not matter. What is important is that they are human beings and we cannot allow this continued oppression, atrocities to be inflicted upon innocent lives,” he stressed.
The prime minister said Malaysia, having experienced colonialism understood the importance of resisting all forms of injustice, thus would continue to support efforts to assist the Palestinian people despite the risks and challenges involved.
He reaffirmed the Madani government’s full commitment to the Palestinian cause and urged all parties to continue contributing their time, effort and resources to help them (Palestinian).
“I know the risks and the problems, but what are they compared with the plight of Palestinian children who are crying out, hoping the world will hear them, yet the world remains deaf.
“It is deeply shameful if we say we cannot do anything because we are too caught up in our own world. So, take the necessary steps, no matter how small the effort, to help the people who have endured 70 years of suffering,” he added.
Anwar also expressed his appreciation to the international participants involved in the Global Sumud Movement, describing them as vital to ensure calls for justice for Palestine continued to resonate internationally.
“It means a lot because you are part of this international movement. But more importantly, you are part of a voice of conscience, of reason, clamoring for justice.
“You don’t show that you are giving up. You show your determination...  you will have a voice of reason, a voice of conscience, a voice that calls for freedom and justice. May Allah guide us,” he added.
Also present were Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari, Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar, Malaysian Consultative Council of Islamic Organisations (Mapim) chief executive officer (CEO) Datuk Dr Sani Araby Abdul Alim Araby, and Malaysian National News Agency (Bernama) CEO Datin Paduka Nur-ul Afida Kamaludin. — Bernama

Title: Student struck and killed by car while crossing road in Miri
Article:
MIRI, Oct 14 — A 16-year-old student was killed after being struck by a car while crossing the road near SMK Luar Bandar Miri in Bekenu on Tuesday.
Miri police chief ACP Mohd Farhan Lee Abdullah said the accident occurred at about 1.10pm when a car driven by a 46-year-old local woman, travelling from Miri towards Bakong, allegedly struck the student.
“The student was pronounced dead at the scene by a medical assistant from Tun Abang Haji Openg Bekenu Health Clinic,” he said in a statement on Tuesday night.
Mohd Farhan said the impact damaged the front-left section of the car, while the driver was unhurt.
He added that the case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for causing death by reckless or dangerous driving.
Meanwhile police have urged anyone with information about the accident to contact investigating officer Insp Mohd Faizal Moktar at 012-818 6509 or 085-430479, or report to the nearest police station. — The Borneo Post

Title: Finance Ministry: RM17.15b in excess tax refunds paid to individuals, companies as of Sept 30
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — The government has settled tax overpayment refunds amounting to RM17.15 billion, involving 3.23 million taxpayer cases, for the period up to September 30, 2026.
According to the Ministry of Finance (MoF), this total included RM6.38 billion being refunded to 3.1 million individual taxpayers and RM8.95 billion being refunded to over 130,000 corporate taxpayers, including micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs).
To strengthen the processing of tax refunds, the Inland Revenue Board has implemented various strategies that are fairer and more equitable, ensuring that refund allocations from the government are distributed in an orderly and effective manner based on the age of outstanding cases, while also prioritising MSMEs and companies facing cash flow issues.
“The government is also committed to ensuring that outstanding refunds are fully settled promptly as part of efforts to enhance tax administration efficiency and safeguard taxpayers' rights, in line with the Madani government’s fiscal reform agenda,” the Ministry of Finance (MoF) said in a written reply published on the parliament website yesterday.
The ministry was replying to a question from Lim Guan Eng (Bagan-PH) regarding the timeframe for settling excess tax refunds and the two per cent compensation for corporate taxpayers for the 2025 year of assessment, as well as the amount of outstanding refunds according to the year of assessment and the number of affected taxpayers. — Bernama

Title: Budget 2027: MPs welcome higher Sabah, Sarawak allocations, call for faster project delivery
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — The increased interim special grants and larger development allocations for Sabah and Sarawak are expected to strengthen development in both states, with Members of Parliament (MPs) hoping this will be followed by a finalised special grant formula and more effective project implementation.
Debating the Supply Bill (Budget) 2027 at the policy stage in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday, Datuk Seri Doris Sophia Brodi (GPS-Sri Aman) said the increase in the interim special grant for both states from RM600 million to RM1.5 billion should be appreciated.
However, she hoped the federal government would expedite the drafting of a final formula that is transparent, objective and sustainable under Article 112D of the Federal Constitution and in line with the spirit of the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63).
Datuk Mohd Kurniawan Naim Moktar (BN-Kinabatangan) urged the government to explain the latest status of negotiations on the formula granting Sabah the right to receive 40 per cent of the net revenue derived by the Federal Government from the state.
“This is not just a matter of additional allocations; it involves constitutional responsibility and fiscal relations between the federal government and the Sabah government.
“Therefore, I ask the government to clarify the latest status of the 40 per cent formula negotiations, the method for verifying the federal net revenue derived from Sabah and the targeted timeline to reach a solution with the state government,” he said.
Meanwhile, Datuk Wetrom Bahanda (KDM-Kota Marudu) proposed that unspent development allocations for Sabah be carried forward to the following year by establishing a Carry Forward Fund.
He said the mechanism would ensure approved allocations continue to be utilised, especially when project implementation faces bureaucratic, technical or other constraints that cause delays.
Wetrom noted that Sabah received an allocation of RM18.7 billion for 2027, an increase of RM1.1 billion from the previous year, but failing to use the entire sum would be detrimental to a state still in need of basic infrastructure development.
Echoing Wetrom’s sentiments, Datuk Seri Wilfred Madius Tangau (GRS-Tuaran) urged the Federal Government to end the culture of announcing development projects that ultimately get delayed and become “sick” projects.
Madius also called for measures to ensure Sabah’s development allocations are fully spent to benefit the people.
He asked the government to detail the amount of Sabah’s 2026 development allocation that had been disbursed and spent, including the value of projects implemented by the Sabah Public Works Department (JKR) and the number of sick projects in the state managed by both Sabah JKR and Federal JKR.
He also proposed five improvement measures, including ensuring land, approval and utility matters are resolved before a project begins, and publicly disclosing physical progress, actual expenditure, completion dates and any extensions of time for projects.
“Sick projects must also have recovery plans and follow-up actions. A second extension of time due to contractor weaknesses should undergo an independent review, including considering contract termination in accordance with the law.
“Additionally, Sabah JKR should be empowered as the technical agency for federal projects valued at RM50 million and below,” he said.
The Dewan Rakyat sitting continues today. — Bernama

Title: Finance Ministry: Malaysians under 30 rack up RM5.4b in BNPL transactions in first half of 2026
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Young people aged 30 and below recorded 65.9 million Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL) transactions worth RM5.4 billion in the first half of 2026, accounting for 37.9 per cent of total BNPL transactions in Malaysia, according to the Ministry of Finance (MoF).
In a written reply published on the parliament website yesterday, the MoF said the total number of BNPL transactions in Malaysia during that period was 173.9 million, valued at RM14.7 billion, with youths contributing 36.7 per cent of the total transaction value.
As of June 30, 2026, the outstanding BNPL financing balance for this demographic stood at RM2.4 billion, while non-performing financing amounted to RM96.8 million, or 4.0 per cent of the outstanding balance.
The MoF was replying to a question from Datuk Dr Alias Razak (Kuala Nerus-PN) regarding measures taken by the Consumer Credit Commission to protect young people from excessive indebtedness through BNPL schemes, including the comprehensive assessment of consumers’ credit commitments. — Bernama

Title: Budget 2027: Technology adoption, business growth key to higher wages, says minister
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — The adoption of technology and business scaling can boost company productivity and enhance the ability to share the gains of growth with employees through wage increases, said Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir.
He noted that efforts to raise productivity to support wage growth must involve not only employees but also the capabilities of employers.
“The current wage increases must be balanced with productivity, not only at the level of the workers themselves but also among employers,” he told Bernama after appearing as a guest on the Bernama TV programme
Ruang Bicara
, titled “Budget 2027: Quality Economic Growth, Prosperous People” yesterday evening.
Akmal Nasrullah said the adoption of technology and financing that supports business scaling are among the ways to strengthen the capabilities of micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs).
“When we speak of the capabilities of MSMEs, we certainly hope they will continue to strengthen their businesses.
“As that scaling-up occurs more effectively and comprehensively, they will be able to share a portion of the growth proceeds with their workers,” he said.
Regarding the sectors targeted for productivity improvements to support wage increases, he said the manufacturing sector needs to move towards more comprehensive technology adoption, rather than relying on low-cost labour, including foreign workers.
He said the initiative aligns with the 13th Malaysia Plan target of reducing reliance on foreign workers from 15 per cent to 10 per cent by the end of the plan period.
“Such sectors certainly need continued encouragement to further enhance their productivity and capabilities,” he said.
According to Akmal Nasrullah, the use of energy-efficient machinery or equipment is also a method for reducing company operating costs.
He noted that government matching grants are available for conducting energy efficiency audits, while details regarding specific funds for technology adoption and productivity enhancement fall under the purview of the relevant ministries. — Bernama

Title: Close, but not caviar: Sushi King wins tax dispute over imported fish roe
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — The seasoned fish eggs commonly served on sushi rolls are culinary garnishes rather than luxury caviar substitutes under customs law, the High Court has ruled.
Judge Norliza Othman dismissed an appeal by the Customs Department director-general against a Customs Appeal Tribunal decision that favoured restaurant chain Sushi King Sdn Bhd regarding the classification of imported tobiko (flying fish roe), masago (capelin roe), and frozen mentaiko (pollock roe),
NST
reported.
The decision confirms that the three products attract zero import duty as prepared or preserved fish, sparing the restaurant operator an 8 per cent tariff imposed on caviar substitutes.
Customs argued that cleaning, seasoning, colouring, and freezing the roe qualified them as caviar substitutes under the Customs Duties Order 2017, contending that consumption methods should not influence tariff classifications.
Sushi King maintained that the roe was imported exclusively as garnishes in Japanese dining and was never marketed or consumed as an alternative to sturgeon caviar.
Norliza agreed, holding that preparation methods alone do not transform everyday fish eggs into a luxury caviar alternative.
“Fish roe is a wide, all-encompassing term used to describe fish eggs, but not all fish roe is caviar or a caviar substitute.
“In this regard, caviar substitute is a very specific subset of fish roe based on its origin, methods of consumption and method of processing, which aims to mimic sturgeon caviar,” she said in written grounds published yesterday.
Citing World Customs Organisation guidelines, the judge held that caviar substitutes must be prepared and consumed in the manner of caviar, concluding that the tribunal had properly assessed the culinary reality of the products before setting aside the department’s tariff rulings.

Title: Budget 2027: Kelantan, Terengganu, Perlis, Kedah, Sabah, Sarawak get RM21.26b development allocation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — The government has allocated RM21.26 billion in development expenditure to six underdeveloped states under Budget 2027, with the distribution taking into account the different needs of each state, said Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir.
He said the six states are Kelantan, Terengganu, Perlis, Kedah, Sabah and Sarawak, with the allocation also reflecting the commitment to infrastructure development and the implementation of previously announced projects.
“There are states that, in terms of infrastructure development for the period we announced, may require a significant commitment. At the same time, this also involves projects that, although not announced this year, will commence implementation this year,” he told Bernama.
He said this after appearing as a guest on Bernama TV’s
Ruang Bicara
programme, titled “Budget 2027: Quality Economic Growth, Prosperous People,” last night.
Akmal Nasrullah said development spending is not only aimed at driving economic growth but also at bridging the development gap between states, including those that are lagging behind.
He said the commitment and allocation for the six states, as stated in the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP), would continue regardless of political differences, in line with the responsibilities of the federal government.
Regarding development spending priorities, Akmal Nasrullah said that, of the total RM83 billion allocated for development under Budget 2027, the focus includes infrastructure development, the creation of economic opportunities and the enhancement of social mobility.
He noted that the development of schools and healthcare facilities, as well as efforts to address the impacts of climate change, are also priorities to ensure that spending delivers high-impact outcomes.
Among the examples given was the commitment to develop a dam in Kelantan to address flooding, as well as steps towards constructing a water treatment plant in Machang.
Earlier in the
Ruang Bicara
programme, he said the Ministry of Economy evaluates development expenditure based on the desired outcomes to ensure that project implementation achieves the intended objectives.
“Sometimes, for example, when implementing a programme or project, even if the project is completed, it can become a white elephant because the planning may have been driven by certain urgent needs. The project is then carried out, but in terms of achieving the objectives we had intended, it does not get very far,” he said.
He said the risks of delays, such as those involving land acquisition and utility relocation, need to be managed more carefully and comprehensively, but these issues should not be used as excuses.
Akmal Nasrullah said the ministry is now evaluating the implementation of preliminary studies before allowing full project applications to proceed, to avoid situations in which issues such as site incompatibility are identified only after a project has been announced.
“If the construction process takes around three years, but the initial phase of identifying the site and so on takes two years, in my opinion, this means the public have to wait an unreasonable length of time for the infrastructure to become available for their use,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Malaysian police trace syndicate behind 521kg syabu seizure in Laos on jet from Subang
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) have identified a syndicate and several individuals believed to be linked to the arrests and drug seizure at Luang Prabang International Airport, Laos, earlier this month.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said investigators had recorded statements from several witnesses, including a Malaysian who acted as a broker who arranged the charter of the aircraft involved.
He said the aircraft had been chartered by a 54-year-old Filipino man, identified as a former pilot with a drug-related criminal record in his home country.
“Investigations have also revealed the involvement of a 51-year-old Filipino woman who is believed to have acted as the syndicate’s coordinator,” he said in a statement yesterday.
Hussein said the case was being handled by the NCID’s Special Investigation Unit under Sections 34 and 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, relating to abetment or preparation in Malaysia for drug trafficking offences committed abroad.
He said the NCID was also working closely with the Foreign Ministry and the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA) to obtain further information and assist in the investigation.
He said the NCID remained committed to combating drugs to protect present and future generations, and urged members of the public with information on drug-related activities to contact the NCID hotline at 012-208 7222.
On October 1, Lao police seized 521 kilograms of crystal methamphetamine from a private Learjet that had arrived from Subang.
Following the incident, 13 individuals, including Malaysian, Singaporean and Filipino nationals, were detained by Lao authorities to assist in investigations into the cross-border drug smuggling case.
On October 7, police arrested a local man who owned the private jet during a raid at Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport in Subang. — Bernama

Title: Three teens injured after flag strikes high-voltage line during Alor Setar procession
Article:
ALOR SETAR, Oct 14 — Three teenage boys were injured by an electric shock after a flag they were carrying during a vegetable temple procession in Mergong, near here, tonight allegedly came into contact with a high-voltage power line.
Mergong Vegetable Temple Association Secretary Chah Boon Chuan said the incident, which occurred at about 9pm, resulted in two 17-year-old victims and one 16-year-old being rushed to Sultanah Bahiyah Hospital (HSB) here.
“The incident happened while thousands of procession participants were marching along the main road in the area before one of the flags allegedly hit the power line. The flag was blown by strong winds during light rain before it was suspected of hitting the power line.
“A teenager holding the flag and two others who were nearby were injured due to the electric shock. All three of them are understood to be receiving treatment in the red zone of HSB,” he said when met at the compound of the HSB Emergency and Trauma Department last night.
He said the three teenagers are still receiving treatment and their current condition is not yet known.
“The pole used to carry the flag was made of bamboo, and this is the first time such an incident has occurred,” he said.
Earlier, several videos went viral on social media regarding the incident, including the condition of the victims lying on the road. — Bernama

Title: Haze continues hitting Johor, Selangor, KL hard: API 177 in Pasir Gudang
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Air quality deteriorated further across the country this morning, with 27 monitoring stations recording unhealthy air pollutant index (API) readings as haze intensified across the central and southern regions of Peninsular Malaysia.
According to Department of Environment (DOE) surveillance data as of 8.54am, 27 out of the nation’s 68 stations registered readings in the unhealthy bracket (API 101 to 200), marking a noticeable increase from the 20 stations reported yesterday morning.
Another 40 stations logged moderate air quality, only one recorded good air quality, and none crossed into the very unhealthy or hazardous categories.
Pasir Gudang in Johor recorded the country's highest reading at 177, easing marginally from 181 yesterday morning. Nilai in Negeri Sembilan saw a sharp overnight spike, jumping from 151 to 174, while Klang and peat fire hotspot Johan Setia in Selangor were tied close behind at 173.
Selangor accounted for five unhealthy stations. Beyond Klang and Johan Setia, elevated readings were recorded in Banting (160), Shah Alam (159), and Petaling Jaya (154).
In Kuala Lumpur, Cheras logged 168 and Batu Muda stood at 164. The administrative centre of Putrajaya rebounded sharply into the unhealthy bracket at 165, up from 120 yesterday morning, breaching the 150-point benchmark used for localized school closure assessments.
Southern and eastern states record rising smoke levels
Johor saw the highest concentration of polluted areas nationwide, with seven stations in the unhealthy band. Following Pasir Gudang, elevated readings were registered in Kota Tinggi (166), Larkin (164), Pengerang (162), Batu Pahat (154), Kluang (152), and Tangkak (151).
In Negeri Sembilan, coastal Port Dickson re-entered the unhealthy register at 165 after dropping out yesterday, while state capital Seremban climbed to 160.
All three monitoring stations in Melaka worsened overnight: Bukit Rambai rose to 169, Bandaraya Melaka stood at 164, and Alor Gajah recorded 156.
On the East Coast, smoke pollution rebounded in Terengganu, with industrial hubs Kemaman and Paka logging 156 and 155 respectively after exiting the list yesterday. In Pahang, Indera Mahkota in Kuantan recorded 155 and Rompin registered 153.
In Sarawak, Serian logged an unhealthy reading of 153, while Sri Aman improved significantly, easing from 170 yesterday to 134 to mark the lowest reading among the 27 affected stations.
Widespread school closures remain in effect
The worsening air quality comes as schools in multiple states remained shut today.
Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek confirmed that all primary and secondary schools across Johor, Melaka, and Negeri Sembilan would stay closed today.
Targeted shutdowns also remain in effect for schools under nine District Education Offices (PPD) nationwide: Hulu Langat and Sepang in Selangor; Kuantan, Pekan, and Rompin in Pahang; Tawau in Sabah; alongside Serian, Sri Aman, and Lubok Antu in Sarawak.
Health and education authorities have urged parents, high-risk groups, and students with respiratory ailments to wear protective face masks outdoors and track real-time hourly API updates via official DOE portals.

Title: Kelantan Social Welfare Dept: Husbands can also be victims of domestic violence
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Oct 14 — Domestic violence does not only involve husbands abusing their wives, but can also involve wives or other family members abusing husbands, said Kelantan Social Welfare Department (JKM) director Che Samsuzuki Che Noh.
He said the issue must be taken seriously as violence within the family could result in serious injuries, death or other criminal acts if left unchecked.
“Sometimes, individuals facing stress may seek an outlet to relieve it, but this should not be done by resorting to violence against their partners or family members,” he told reporters after the opening ceremony of the 2026 Kelantan State JKM Temporary Evacuation Centre Management Training and Simulation Exercise here yesterday.
Che Samsuzuki said 32 domestic violence cases had been recorded in Kelantan so far this year, including the latest incident involving a woman who was seriously injured after being stabbed by her husband in Kampung Padang Lepai, Kadok, on October 5.
In this regard, he said JKM would continue working with the Kelantan State Women’s Development Office, the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) and relevant agencies to raise public awareness of domestic violence and the assistance available to victims.
Victims of abuse are urged to seek help from JKM or the Women’s Development Office, as well as lodge a police report and undergo a medical examination if they have sustained injuries, he said.
“Do not remain silent or regard it merely as a family matter. Victims need to seek help so that appropriate action can be taken and their safety ensured,” he said. — Bernama
* If you are experiencing domestic violence, the following hotlines offer free and confidential support: Talian Kasih at 15999 or WhatsApp 019-2615999 (24/7); All Women’s Action Society at 016-2374221/ 016-2284221 (9.30am-5.30pm); and Women’s Aid Organisation (WAO) at 03-30008858 or SMS/WhatsApp TINA 018-9888058 (24/7).

Title: ‘False report’: Indonesian student, not Malaysian, held in Tanjung Balai 4kg syabu case, says Bukit Aman
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) denied reports in a local newspaper and on social media claiming a Malaysian university student was arrested for smuggling over four kilogrammes of syabu in Tanjung Balai, Indonesia, on October 10.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said investigations found that the suspect arrested by the republic’s authorities is a 21-year-old Indonesian man.
He said the suspect, from Medan, is a student at a higher learning institution in Indonesia.
Hussein said the drugs were obtained from a syndicate in Malaysia before being smuggled out.
“Further investigations revealed the drugs were handed over by another Indonesian man in the Klang Valley to be brought to Indonesia via the Tanjung Balai Ferry Terminal,” he said in a statement yesterday.
The suspect was arrested by Tanjung Balai Police (POLRES) at 5pm local time on October 10 after arriving at the Teluk Nibung Ferry Terminal in Tanjung Balai on a ferry from Port Dickson, Negeri Sembilan.
Hussein said an X-ray scan of the man’s luggage found eight plastic packets suspected to contain methamphetamine, weighing 4.044 kilogrammes.
He stressed that the report titled “Lagi kes rakyat Malaysia ditahan, pelajar universiti ‘kantoi’ seludup 4kg syabu” is untrue and could cause confusion and concern among the public.
“NCID urges relevant parties not to spread any news without verified facts and to obtain prior confirmation from the authorities,” he said.
He said NCID takes cross-border smuggling seriously and will continue to cooperate with the Indonesian National Police (POLRI).
He said the cooperation aims to gather intelligence to identify the supply source and dismantle drug syndicate networks in Malaysia linked to the case.
The public with information on the case is urged to channel it through the NCID hotline at 012-208 7222. — Bernama

Title: Sabah diesel aid covers 52,133 pickup, SUV owners under Budi Diesel scheme
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — A total of 52,133 owners of diesel vehicles such as pickups and sport utility vehicles (SUVs) in Sabah have been approved for an additional 100 litres of diesel under the Budi Madani Diesel (Budi Diesel) programme as of October 12, 2026, said the Ministry of Finance (MoF).
The ministry said the additional eligibility criteria take into account the higher diesel consumption needs, particularly among rural residents, small traders, farmers and those who use diesel vehicles to generate income.
In addition, a total of 19,008 Budi Diesel eligibility transfer applications have been approved, with 5,555 of them involving applicants from Sabah.
MoF noted that the government implemented the diesel subsidy targeting reform through Budi Diesel in phases beginning June 27, 2026, before expanding its implementation nationwide on July 1, 2026.
The ministry said this in response to a question from Vivian Wong Shir Yee (Sandakan-PH) regarding the diesel subsidy mechanism in Sabah in a written answer published on the Parliament’s website yesterday.
For users other than individual vehicle owners, MoF said the government also considers the needs of certain groups that rely on diesel for daily use, including boat operators as well as users of electric generators (gensets) and water pumps in rural areas.
It pointed out that these groups could be considered for Budi Diesel assistance through the MyKad mechanism, subject to eligibility requirements and verification by the state government and relevant agencies, such as district offices, resident offices or designated state agencies.
The measure aims to ensure that groups that truly rely on diesel to meet their daily needs do not miss out on receiving assistance.
“The government will continue to monitor the implementation of BUDI Diesel based on usage data, user feedback, input from the state government and the needs of the sectors involved.
“Any improvements will be refined through data so that diesel subsidies can be channelled more easily, fairly, in a more targeted and sustainable manner to users who truly qualify, without opening up opportunities for leakage or abuse of subsidies,” MoF added. — Bernama

Title: Violent Kota Damansara thunderstorm: Viral clip shows wind lifting car at toll plaza (VIDEO)
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — A dramatic video capturing the terrifying moment violent storm winds appeared to lift a car and toss it into another vehicle near a toll plaza in Kota Damansara has gone viral on social media.
The footage, shared online at around 6.30pm yesterday, shows what witnesses described as a waterspout or freak whirlwind striking motorists queuing along the toll lanes amid blinding rain and howling gusts.
In the clip, the powerful vortex lifts the rear of a stationary car waiting to approach the toll barrier, shoving it forcefully into an adjacent vehicle.
Both cars sustained minor body damage in the collision. Subsequent reports indicated that no injuries were sustained by either driver or their passengers.
