The incident unfolded during a severe evening downpour that battered several parts of Selangor and the Klang Valley, snarling rush-hour traffic.
Prior to the storm, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) had issued a regional thunderstorm advisory forecasting heavy downpours, lightning, and gusty winds across multiple peninsular states heading into the peak evening commute.

Title: In Dewan Rakyat today: Alibaba licences, Gaza and troubled housing project among focus
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Legislation to curb “Alibaba” licensing practices, Malaysia’s diplomatic efforts on Gaza and the fate of an abandoned housing project are among the key issues expected to be raised in the Dewan Rakyat today.
According to the Order Paper, Syahredzan Johan (PH-Bangi) will ask the Economy Minister about the status of drafting the Anti-Rent-Seeking Act and the timeline for its tabling in Parliament to curb “Alibaba” licensing practices.
The West Asia conflict is also expected to feature prominently, with Ahmad Tarmizi Sulaiman (PN-Sik) asking the Foreign Minister about Malaysia’s diplomatic efforts at the United Nations (UN) and the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) to ensure that the ceasefire and humanitarian aid to Gaza continue.
Also drawing attention is the fate of 1,120 residential units at the Residensi Wilayah Salak Selatan apartment project, with Fong Kui Lun (PH-Bukit Bintang) asking the Housing and Local Government Ministry to explain its rescue plan, including a proposal to appoint a rescue developer if the Scheme of Arrangement fails.
Meanwhile, Jimmy Puah Wee Tse (PH-Tebrau) will raise preparations for workforce transition plans in response to the threat posed by artificial intelligence (AI), while Suhaizan Kaiat (PH-Pulai) will ask about median wages and graduates working in jobs below their academic qualifications (underemployment).
Other matters on the agenda include the future direction of the Tabung Pahlawan, with Nordin Ahmad Ismail (PN-Lumut) asking the Defence Minister to explain its transformation; the distribution of aid to Sekolah Agama Rakyat in 2026, raised by Datuk Ahmad Saad @ Yahaya (PN-Pokok Sena); and agricultural input costs and bushfires on Pulau Bruit, Sarawak, raised by Sabri Azit (PN-Jerai).
After the question-and-answer session, the Dewan Rakyat will consider a motion to appoint Members of Parliament to the Parliamentary Services Council, to be tabled by the Prime Minister.
Under the motion, two government MPs, Ramkarpal Singh (PH-Bukit Gelugor) and Datuk Seri Hasni Mohammad (BN-Simpang Renggam), and two opposition MPs, Datuk Seri Dr Ronald Kiandee (PN-Beluran) and Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan (PN-Kota Bharu), will be nominated to serve on the council in accordance with Section 3(2)(f) of the Parliamentary Services Act 2025.
The Dewan Rakyat will then continue debating the Supply Bill 2027 at the policy stage, following the tabling of Budget 2027 by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also Finance Minister, last Friday.
According to the calendar for the Third Meeting of the Fifth Session of the 15th Parliament, the policy-stage debate on Budget 2027 runs from October 12 to 22, before ministers deliver their winding-up speeches over four days beginning October 26.
The Dewan Rakyat sitting runs for 37 days until December 8. — Bernama

Title: Multi-lane fast flow: What motorists need to know as Malaysia moves towards barrier-free tolling
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Malaysia is moving towards multi-lane fast flow (MLFF), a tolling system that would eventually allow motorists to pay tolls without stopping at conventional toll plazas.
As part of that transition, two systems are now being introduced to motorists: PLUS’ JustGo and Touch ’n Go’s Titan Flow.
They are not quite the same thing.
JustGo is a digital toll payment system that uses automatic number plate recognition (ANPR) to identify a vehicle and charge the debit or credit card linked to the motorist’s account.
Titan Flow, meanwhile, is Touch ’n Go’s broader MLFF technology platform, combining Radio Frequency Identification (RFID), ANPR, Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) and artificial intelligence.
For now, motorists will encounter the technology mainly through Enhanced RFID lanes, rather than as a standalone service or a huge gantry on a highway called Titan Flow.
So how do these systems work, how can motorists use them, and what happens if something goes wrong?
JustGo is a digital toll payment system that uses automatic number plate recognition (ANPR) to identify a vehicle and charge the debit or credit card linked to the motorist’s account. — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin
JustGo
JustGo is essentially a camera-based toll payment system.
Once a vehicle is registered with JustGo, cameras at participating toll plazas read its number plate and match it to the motorist’s account.
The toll is then charged to the linked debit or credit card.
Motorists do not need an RFID tag specifically to use JustGo.
To sign up, users first download the JustGo app and register their phone number and email address.
They then have to complete the electronic Know Your Customer (e-KYC) verification using their MyKad, MyTentera or passport, including a real-time selfie and liveness check.
The next step is the electronic Know Your Vehicle (e-KYV), which requires the vehicle’s photographs and ownership documents.
A debit or credit card can then be linked to the account for toll payments.
Once everything is completed, the app should display the registered number plate and linked payment method, with the ANPR status shown as “ACTIVE”.
Users can register up to 10 vehicles.
Vehicles that are not registered in the user’s name can also be added, although supporting documents and manual approval may be required.
JustGo currently supports Class 1 vehicles, broadly covering passenger cars such as sedans, SUVs, MPVs and small pick-ups.
PLUS activated JustGo across participating toll plazas on its highways in August.
In its FAQ, it stated that JustGo is exclusively available at all lanes at all toll plazas on PLUS highways.
There are some location-specific exceptions, including the U-turn at the Tanjung Kupang Toll Plaza, while at the Bandar Cassia Toll Plaza, only RFID lanes are currently activated for ANPR.
The coverage is subject to change, so motorists should check the latest information from JustGo or PLUS before travelling.
In normal operation, the process is simple: drive into a participating lane, the camera reads the number plate, the system matches the vehicle to the registered account and the toll is charged to the linked bank card.
In normal operation, the process is simple: drive into a participating lane, the camera reads the number plate, the system matches the vehicle to the registered account and the toll is charged to the linked bank card. — Picture by Hari Anggara
According to JustGo’s FAQ, motorists cannot simply pay cash at the exit if the linked card has insufficient funds.
It stated that drivers must ensure they have sufficient funds in their bank card before the start of their journey.
“If you are mid-way in your journey, kindly pull aside in a safe area i.e. a rest and relax area (R&R) to top-up your bank card safely,” the FAQ stated.
If the vehicle becomes stuck at a toll lane, motorists should use the intercom to seek assistance.
There is also a specific situation in which a JustGo user may see a Touch ’n Go eWallet deduction instead of a bank-card charge.
This can happen if the ANPR system fails to detect the vehicle at the previous entry point, meaning the toll cannot be charged to the linked bank card and is instead deducted from the linked Touch ’n Go eWallet.
Touch ’n Go describes Titan Flow as a next-generation MLFF platform that combines several technologies, including RFID, ANPR, LiDAR and artificial intelligence, together with open-payment capabilities. — Picture by Yusof Mat Isa
Titan Flow
Touch ’n Go describes Titan Flow as a next-generation MLFF platform that combines several technologies, including RFID, ANPR, LiDAR and artificial intelligence, together with open-payment capabilities.
In practical terms, however, motorists cannot currently download a “Titan Flow” app and start using it as a separate toll payment service.
Instead, elements of the technology are already being introduced through Enhanced RFID lanes.
Enhanced RFID still uses the physical Touch ’n Go RFID tag attached to the vehicle. Existing RFID tags can be used, meaning motorists do not need to obtain a special “Titan Flow” or “enhanced RFID” tag.
The basic process remains familiar to existing RFID users: obtain a Touch ’n Go RFID tag, register and activate it with the vehicle and link it to a Touch ’n Go eWallet account.
When the vehicle enters an Enhanced RFID lane, the system detects the RFID tag and the toll is deducted from the linked eWallet.
When the vehicle enters an Enhanced RFID lane, the system detects the RFID tag and the toll is deducted from the linked eWallet. — Picture by Hari Anggara
The important difference is that Enhanced RFID is part of the technology being developed towards MLFF, with additional detection and identification capabilities being tested alongside the existing RFID system.
It is just the same system as normal RFID, but the toll lane setup has been improved for faster, more reliable vehicle detection at higher speeds.
So these technological improvements could reduce the “
Reverse, Forward, InsyaAllah Detect
” problem at the toll booth.
For motorists, the easiest way to tell whether they are entering an Enhanced RFID lane is to look for the designated Enhanced RFID signage, including the gold star marking.
The first Enhanced RFID deployment was at the Dato Keramat Toll Plaza on the Ampang-Kuala Lumpur Elevated Highway (AKLEH), while another was subsequently introduced at the Putrajaya-bound toll plaza on the Maju Expressway (MEX).
Touch ’n Go has also announced plans for 10 more Enhanced RFID lanes by the end of 2026, covering highways including MEX, the Kajang Dispersal Link Expressway (SILK), Grand Sepadu, Guthrie Corridor Expressway (GCE) and the East Klang Valley Expressway (EKVE).
Unlike the long-term MLFF concept with no barriers, these are still designated toll lanes.
Motorists must continue to follow the lane markings and signage rather than assuming that every part of the highway has already become barrier-free. — Picture by Firdaus Latif
Motorists must therefore continue to follow the lane markings and signage rather than assuming that every part of the highway has already become barrier-free.
So, in simple terms, JustGo identifies your vehicle through its number plate and charges a linked debit or credit card.
Enhanced RFID identifies your vehicle through an RFID tag and deducts the toll from a linked Touch ’n Go eWallet.
Titan Flow is the wider technology platform that Touch ’n Go is developing for the eventual MLFF system, rather than a separate consumer app that motorists currently need to sign up for.
The two systems are part of Malaysia’s wider transition towards barrier-free tolling, but motorists do not currently have to choose between “JustGo” and “Titan Flow” as two competing nationwide payment systems.
For now, JustGo can be used at participating PLUS toll plazas where ANPR has been activated, while Touch ’n Go users can encounter the newer Titan Flow technology through designated Enhanced RFID lanes.
The eventual aim of MLFF is to remove the need for conventional toll lanes altogether, allowing vehicles to be identified and charged while continuing their journey.

Title: Police: Two investigation papers opened over RM350,000 bribery claim against senior MACC officer
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — Two separate investigation papers have been opened into allegations that a senior Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) officer received a bribe of RM350,000 from an individual in 2017.
Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department (CID) director Datuk M. Kumar said the investigations were initiated following a police report lodged over the matter, which had gone viral on several social media platforms.
He said the first investigation paper was opened under Section 165 of the Penal Code, which deals with public servants accepting valuable items without consideration from persons connected to their official duties.
“If convicted, offenders face imprisonment for up to two years, a fine, or both,” he said in a statement today.
Kumar said the investigation is being conducted under Section 500 of the Penal Code for defamation, which carries a maximum penalty of two years’ jail, a fine, or both upon conviction.
He said police are also investigating possible offences under Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 for the improper use of network facilities or services and carries a fine of up to RM500,000, imprisonment of up to two years, or both, upon conviction.
Kumar said police would also submit an application for an Order to Investigate under Section 108(2) of the Criminal Procedure Code to the Public Prosecutor to facilitate further investigations.
“This includes recording witness statements and obtaining confirmation of the status of previous investigations conducted by the MACC,” he said.
He urged the public not to speculate on the case and advised them to use social media responsibly to safeguard the country’s peace and security.
On Saturday (October 10), Malaysian Corruption Watch (MCW) urged the MACC and the Anti-Corruption Advisory Board (ACAB) to promptly investigate the allegations involving the senior officer to safeguard the agency’s integrity.
The case had previously been investigated by the MACC in 2018 but the investigation was closed after no wrongdoing was proven. — Bernama

Title: Myanmar refugees convicted of offences must serve sentence in Malaysia before repatriation, says Saifuddin Nasution
Article:
SUNGAI PETANI, Oct 13 — Myanmar refugees convicted of criminal offences must complete their sentences in this country before being repatriated to their home country.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said although the Myanmar government is prepared to accept back its citizens currently held in Immigration detention depots here, screening will be conducted first before such action is taken.
“The Myanmar government has agreed to accept back its citizens who are here following our screening process, if our records show they were involved in legal violations, we will handle the legal proceedings first,” he said.
He told reporters after the Madani Townhall programme for Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) Kedah students with the Home Minister here today.
He added that, based on the initial commitment agreed upon by both parties, 5,000 Myanmar refugees are set to be repatriated.
“We have identified 5,000 refugees and processed 1,400, sending them back by sea... the remaining 3,600 Myanmar nationals are expected to be repatriated in stages subsequently,” he said.
On October 8, Myanmar expressed its readiness to accept the repatriation of up to another 4,000 of its citizens currently held in Immigration detention depots in this country.
This matter was announced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim following a bilateral meeting with Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing at Bangunan Perdana Putra in Putrajaya. — Bernama

Title: Anwar calls for stronger federal-state cooperation under National Covenant framework
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — The federal and state governments must strengthen cooperation under the proposed National Covenant framework to ensure more sustainable, equitable and balanced development, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
He said the framework, outlined in Budget 2027, was a key focus of the 150th Meeting of Menteri Besar and Chief Ministers, which he chaired today.
The proposed covenant aims to strengthen federal-state cooperation and promote more inclusive development and public well-being.
“Amid global economic uncertainties, national growth projections and fluctuations in global oil prices, the budget must continue to protect the people, address the rising cost of living and take into account each state’s priorities, including border security, particularly in Sabah and Sarawak,” he said in a Facebook post today.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, stressed the importance of aligning development plans and allocations with actual needs on the ground, saying that priority must be given to improving public service delivery, infrastructure development, strengthening state economies and implementing projects that directly benefit the people.
Other than that, the Prime Minister said the meeting also discussed the importance of post-quantum cryptography in strengthening the protection of national data and digital systems against emerging technological challenges and future cybersecurity threats.
On transboundary haze, Anwar said Indonesia had been urged to take immediate and effective action against open burning.
He said decisive measures were necessary as the haze threatened public health, particularly that of schoolchildren, and disrupted schooling.
As of 3pm today, 22 areas nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings, prompting the closure of all schools in Johor, Melaka and Negeri Sembilan tomorrow (October 14).
Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said in a Facebook post that the closures would also affect schools in several districts in Selangor, Pahang, Sabah and Sarawak.
Schools in all other states and districts will operate as usual. — Bernama

Title: Cross-border haze to ease in two weeks as monsoon transition begins, says deputy minister
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — The cross-border haze that has affected Malaysia’s air quality since August 8 is expected to gradually subside over the next two weeks as wind patterns change, Deputy Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Syed Ibrahim Syed Noh said.
He said Malaysia had entered the monsoon transition phase on October 9, with the northeast monsoon expected to begin towards the end of this month.
“However, I want to emphasise that changes in weather conditions alone are not a long-term solution to the haze issue. It could happen again.
“Fire prevention efforts must therefore address the problem at its source. Domestic enforcement must be strengthened, while regional cooperation must be enhanced to reduce the risk of similar incidents recurring,” he said during the Special Chamber session in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Syed Ibrahim was responding to concerns raised by Khoo Poay Tiong (PH-Kota Melaka), who described the haze as a national crisis affecting public health, safety, the economy and public well-being.
The issue was also raised by Dr Kelvin Yii Lee Wuen (PH-Bandar Kuching) and Young Syefura Othman (PH-Bentong).
Yii said the haze was no longer merely a seasonal nuisance but an annual emergency requiring stronger action, including the proposed introduction of a Cross-Border Haze Pollution Act and greater transparency in sharing hotspot data and information on plantation concessions.
Young Syefura, meanwhile, sought clarification on the government’s diplomatic engagements with Indonesia, including the responses received and the effectiveness of the measures taken.
She also called for stronger domestic enforcement and better protection for vulnerable groups.
In his response, Syed Ibrahim said the latest haze episode was caused by an increase in forest and land fires in several parts of Indonesia, including Kalimantan and Sumatra, which had affected air quality in Malaysia, particularly in Sarawak.
He said the Department of Environment (DOE) received 2,104 complaints concerning open burning and carried out 3,039 enforcement actions between August 3 and October 9.
These comprised 2,104 monitoring actions, 168 field orders, 32 notices, 13 compounds and two court actions.
As part of the mitigation efforts, the government also conducted 11 cloud seeding operations between August 30 and October 15 in collaboration with the Malaysian Meteorological Department, the National Disaster Management Agency and the Malaysian Army.
“The main challenge in enforcing laws with cross-border elements is obtaining sufficient evidence to establish the source of pollution and identify the parties responsible,” he said.
Syed Ibrahim added that the ministry had yet to receive any official information from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs or the Ministry of Plantation and Commodities regarding the alleged involvement of Malaysian companies in open-burning incidents in Indonesia. — Bernama

Title: Haze: Kedah schools to operate as usual tomorrow as API readings remain moderate
Article:
ALOR SETAR, Oct 13 — All schools in Kedah will operate as usual tomorrow, with Air Pollutant Index (API) readings across the state remaining below 100 as of 2pm today.
In a statement, the Kedah State Education Department (JPN) said any decisions on school closures or reopening due to the haze would be subject to the Education Ministry’s directives, based on JPN’s monitoring of daily API readings and local developments.
“Kedah JPN will continue to monitor the situation and coordinate with the District Education Offices and schools to safeguard the health, safety and well-being of students and education personnel,” it added. — Bernama

Title: Home Ministry to seek details on five Malaysians held in Japan drug bust, says Saifuddin Nasution
Article:
SUNGAI PETANI, Oct 13 — The Home Ministry will contact Japanese authorities to obtain accurate information on the arrest of Malaysians suspected of involvement in a drug case in Japan.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said he had instructed Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan to act immediately to establish the facts.
“Complete information on the incident will be conveyed to the media as soon as it is received,” he told reporters after the Madani Townhall session between Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) Kedah students and the Home Minister here today.
He was commenting on the arrest of five Malaysians, including a woman, at Haneda Airport in Tokyo last Saturday on suspicion of attempting to smuggle about five kilogrammes (kg) of cocaine worth ¥120 million (RM3.1 million).
According to Fuji News Network (FNN), the operation was uncovered after customs officers became suspicious of a suspect wearing shoes with unusually thick soles.
FNN reported that the suspects were believed to have concealed the drugs beneath their shoe insoles when boarding a flight from Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA), before customs inspections upon arrival in Japan exposed the alleged smuggling attempt.
Saifuddin Nasution said the Home Ministry’s move was also in line with the approach taken in the case involving the arrest of a Malaysian co-pilot in Jakarta several months ago, as well as the seizure of 521 kg of drugs from a private jet in Laos, which was initially alleged to have originated from Malaysia.
Meanwhile, he said the implementation of 17 recommendations or initiatives undertaken through a joint committee comprising the Home Ministry and the Transport Ministry (MOT) to strengthen security at KLIA and the country’s entry points would continue as planned.
He said the initiatives would be implemented in three phases, with the first focusing on destinations identified as high-risk areas or hotspots.
“For destinations listed as hotspots, comprehensive screening of passengers, including body and baggage checks, will be carried out on 100 per cent of passengers,” he said.
However, he said destinations in Japan, including Tokyo, were not included in the original list of hotspots. — Bernama

Title: Businessman sentenced to six months’ jail, ordered to pay RM5,000 for assaulting ex-girlfriend
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Oct 13 — A businessman was sentenced to six months’ jail by the Magistrate’s Court here today for assaulting his former girlfriend, causing injuries to her eyes and body, two years ago.
Magistrate Amira Sariaty Zainal imposed the sentence on Hoh Peng Onn, 47, after the defence failed to raise reasonable doubt at the end of the defence case.
“The court orders that the prison sentence take effect from the date of conviction today. The accused must also pay RM5,000 in compensation to the victim, taking into account the trauma, injuries and emotional distress she suffered,” Amira Sariaty said.
The court also ordered that Hoh serve an additional two months in jail if he failed to pay the compensation today.
However, the court allowed an application by defence counsel Cheow Wee to stay the prison sentence pending an appeal to the High Court, but ordered that the compensation be paid today.
Hoh was charged with intentionally causing hurt to Liaw Ju Shuang, 28, at a residence in Putra Permai Town Centre, Seri Kembangan, at 12.30am on October 5, 2024.
The charge was brought under Section 323 of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum jail term of one year, a fine of up to RM2,000, or both.
In her judgment, Amira Sariaty said that although the neighbour, the third prosecution witness, did not witness the assault, the witness saw the victim with a bleeding head and bruises around her eyes and other parts of her body when she sought help.
“The witness also contacted the police, who took the victim to hospital for treatment. There was no reason for the victim to fabricate a story to frame the accused.
“In view of this, the court finds that the defence failed to raise reasonable doubt against the prosecution’s case, and was merely a denial unsupported by strong evidence and testimony,” Amira Sariaty said.
During mitigation, the defence sought a fine, citing the accused’s eyesight problems, which it said would make imprisonment difficult for him.
However, Deputy Public Prosecutor Syed Ahmed Khabir Abdul Rahman sought a jail term and a fine, arguing that the public interest outweighed that of the accused, given the extent of the victim’s injuries, and requested that compensation be awarded to her. — Bernama

Title: Budget 2027: Malaysia’s 3.3pc fiscal deficit target achievable, says Tengku Zafrul
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — Malaysia is capable of achieving its fiscal deficit target of 3.3 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP) under Budget 2027, provided the assumptions underpinning the budget hold amid global economic and geopolitical uncertainties, said Datuk Seri Tengku Zafrul Abdul Aziz.
The Malaysian Investment Development Authority (Mida) chairman, who is also a senior political advisor to the Prime Minister and a former Finance Minister, noted that the country’s fiscal position had improved over the past three years.
“When we look at the fiscal discipline that we have demonstrated over the last three years, with the fiscal deficit at around 5.5 per cent in 2022, we are moving in the right direction.
“If we look at government revenue and the country’s GDP growth, we should be able to achieve the 3.3 per cent target, provided the global geopolitical situation, the various challenges facing the world, oil prices and the other assumptions underpinning the budget remain as expected,” Tengku Zafrul said to Bernama.
He described Budget 2027 as a responsible budget that balances investment incentives with efforts to ensure that economic growth benefits a wider segment of Malaysians and businesses.
He noted that the budget took into account the interests of different stakeholders, while seeking to strengthen economic growth and ensure that its benefits reached both lower-income groups and businesses.
“If you look at it objectively, it is a well-thought-out and balanced budget that takes into account the interests of all stakeholders while ensuring that both the lower- and higher-income groups are supported,” he said.
On investment prospects, Tengku Zafrul said planned capital expenditure by government-linked investment companies (GLICs) and government-linked companies (GLCs) could generate positive spillover effects for the broader economy.
He said investments by Khazanah Nasional Bhd, the Employees Provident Fund and other institutions, as well as capital expenditure by Petronas sent positive signals to potential investors, as domestic investment commitments could help strengthen foreign investors’ confidence in Malaysia.
“I believe that these are good for investors to take note of, because when they come to invest in a country, they also want to see confidence, and if our own companies or institutions are investing, then they will also be more comfortable or more confident in doing so,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Senior govt agency official, company director remanded seven days in bribery probe
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — A senior official of a government agency and a company director have been remanded for seven days for allegedly soliciting and receiving bribes totalling about RM15,000.
The bribes were believed to be an inducement to secure supply work at the government agency.
Magistrate Aliaa Anwar issued the remand order against both men, effective from today until Oct 19, following an application by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) at the Kuala Lumpur Magistrate’s Court this morning.
It is understood that both suspects, in their 50s and 60s, were detained at 2pm yesterday when they went to give their statements at the Kuala Lumpur MACC office.
Preliminary investigations revealed that the suspects allegedly colluded in the act between 2021 and 2023.
Meanwhile, Kuala Lumpur MACC director Mohammad Zakkuan Talib, when contacted, confirmed the remand.
He said the case is being investigated under Section 17(a) of the MACC Act 2009. — Bernama

Title: STAM and MUET examinations in Pahang to continue as planned despite haze
Article:
KUANTAN, Oct 13 — The Sijil Tinggi Agama Malaysia (STAM) and Malaysian University English Test (MUET) examinations in Pahang will proceed as scheduled despite the haze.
In a statement, the Pahang State Education Department (JPN) said the examinations would be conducted in accordance with the standard operating procedures (SOP) and safety measures in force.
“Students attending school, including those sitting for ongoing examinations, are encouraged to wear face masks to protect their health,” it said.
Candidates and examination personnel were advised to refer to their schools, examination centres and the department’s official channels for further notifications and instructions.
Meanwhile, all educational institutions under Pahang JPN in Rompin, Pekan and Kuantan will be closed tomorrow due to the haze affecting the districts.
The department said any changes to the operational status of educational institutions and their reopening would be announced through its official channels and the respective District Education Offices, based on prevailing conditions and safety considerations.
Pahang JPN will continue to monitor the situation in coordination with the three district education offices and relevant agencies to safeguard the health, safety and well-being of students and education personnel. — Bernama

Title: Teachers union: RM69b education allocation must bring real improvements to Malaysian schools
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — Better school facilities, improved safety and a more conducive learning environment are among the key improvements the school community hopes to see from the increased allocation for education in Budget 2027.
West Malaysia Malay Teachers Union (KGMMB) president Dr Mohd Sobri Yusuf said the RM69 billion allocation, up from RM66.2 billion this year, should translate into meaningful improvements in schools, with its success measured by the actual benefits delivered to teachers and students.
“Regardless of how much is allocated, the desired outcomes will not be achieved unless the funding brings about positive and tangible changes,” he said on Bernama TV’s Apa Khabar Malaysia talk show today.
Mohd Sobri said the higher school maintenance allocation, which has doubled to RM2 billion, could deliver direct benefits to school communities, particularly in ensuring that learning facilities were safe and comfortable.
“Safety must come first, and maintenance funds should go to schools that need them most, especially for repairs such as leaking roofs and faulty wiring, so that students and teachers can learn and work in a safe and comfortable environment,” he said.
Mohd Sobri said the recruitment of 200 teaching assistants for primary schools with large numbers of pupils could help reduce teachers’ workload, allowing them to focus more on teaching and students’ learning needs.
On the Supplementary Food Programme (RMT), he said its implementation must be closely monitored to ensure students received meals that met the required quality standards and complied with the prescribed menu and portion sizes.
Meanwhile, Federation of Peninsular Malay Students (GPMS) president Muhd Fazreen Ismadi Fauzi said increasing the Early Schooling Assistance (BAP) to RM200 would help parents, particularly those from the B40 group, meet the cost of preparing their children for school.
However, he stressed that the increase in aid should be accompanied by measures to keep school supplies affordable and provide lasting relief to families.
On the RM2,500 allowance for Form Six students, Muhd Fazreen suggested that the aid be disbursed monthly rather than in a lump sum, allowing students to manage their educational expenses more effectively throughout the year.
“For GPMS, it would be better to pay the allowance monthly rather than in one lump sum. If students receive the full amount at once, they might spend it in a day on things like mobile phones, and the money may not last them through the year,” he said.
He added that aid distribution must be closely monitored to ensure the funds reach the intended recipients without any leakage.
Muhd Fazreen also stressed the need to ensure school facilities cater to students with disabilities, particularly with the planned enrolment of six-year-olds in Year One from 2027.
He said schools must be equipped with suitable facilities and support services to meet the needs of all students. — Bernama

Title: Fahmi proposes initiative to preserve speeches, writings of Malaysia’s founding leaders
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil today has proposed a national initiative to preserve and revive historical speeches and writings of Malaysia’s founding leaders for future generations.
He said the initiative, inspired by the reprint of pioneering journalist J. Victor Morais’ Great Wisdom of the First Malaysians, could involve retrieving rare speeches, writings and historical accounts from archives.
“I will discuss with National Unity Minister (Datuk Aaron Ago Dagang) to identify the most appropriate steps. If possible, we will work towards organising something in conjunction with National Month celebrations next year.”
Fahmi said this at the launch of Great Wisdom of the First Malaysians – A Reprint of Selected Speeches by Pioneering Journalist J. Victor Morais here today.
Also present were Malaysian National News Agency (Bernama) editor-in-chief Arul Rajoo Durar Raj, Daily Express chief editor Datuk Sardahthisa James and Victor’s son Benedict Morais.
Fahmi said the collection highlighted the importance of preserving the intellectual contributions and perspectives of the country’s founding figures, particularly at a time when rapid development and the pursuit of future progress could overshadow an understanding of the nation’s past.
The communications minister said the book deserved wider circulation beyond its initial print run of 2,000 copies to ensure its valuable historical content reached a broader audience.
In this regard, Fahmi offered to help raise funds to print an additional 2,000 copies, subject to the agreement of those involved in the publication, and proposed organising a related programme at Parliament next year.
He said he would distribute copies to all Cabinet ministers at Friday’s meeting to highlight the importance of understanding Malaysia’s nation-building history.
Meanwhile, Sardahthisa, also known as James Sarda, said the book provided valuable insights into the aspirations of Malaysia’s founding leaders and the challenges they faced during the country’s formation, making it an important resource for researchers, policymakers and younger generations.
He collaborated with Benedict to republish the collection, originally released in 1967 under the title Selected Speeches.
“For journalists like me, finding speeches delivered by Tunku Abdul Rahman and Tun Abdul Razak in Parliament is not easy, as record-keeping was different in those days and access to parliamentary records involved various protocols.
“This book is a gold mine for research. It is a one-stop centre containing the speeches of leaders from various backgrounds and their hopes for Malaysia,” he told reporters after the event.
Meanwhile, Benedict recalled that his father was a self-taught journalist who honed his skills through a correspondence course at Rapid Results College (RRC) in London at a time when formal journalism training was not widely available.
The 80-year-old said his father later gained practical experience through on-the-job training, reflecting the determination and initiative that shaped his career in journalism.
Recalling the declaration of independence on Aug 31, 1957, Benedict said he was a 12-year-old student among the 25,000 people who witnessed the historic occasion at Merdeka Stadium, including Tunku Abdul Rahman’s seven resounding cries of “Merdeka”.
He also recalled the strong sense of unity among the people during that period, when they simply identified themselves as Malayans regardless of race.
“We saw ourselves as Malayans…neighbours kept their homes open, shared food and visited one another freely. It was a spirit of unity that came naturally rather than being imposed,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Orang Asli children should not be denied documentation over parents’ marriage records, says National Registration Dept
Article:
GUA MUSANG, Oct 13 — Orang Asli children should not be left without documentation because of issues involving their parents’ marriage records, said National Registration Department (JPN) director-general Datuk Badrul Hisham Alias.
He said JPN would assess each case based on the facts, supporting documents and individual circumstances to determine the appropriate action, particularly for birth registration.
He said the department respected the customs and culture of the Orang Asli community, but customary marriages and the legal requirements for marriage registration had to be assessed in accordance with the applicable laws.
“Children should not be left without documentation assistance just because their parents face marriage record issues. We respect customs, obey the law and help find solutions,” he told reporters after attending the Registration Literacy Programme held in conjunction with the 78th state-level National Registration Day celebration at Pos Balar here.
Badrul Hisham said each case had to be assessed individually, with no automatic conclusions drawn about the recognition of customary marriages without considering the specific facts and circumstances.
He said 143 New Generation MyKads had been issued to the Orang Asli community in Kelantan through the MEKAR Programme, which brings registration services closer to the community.
He clarified that the figure referred only to MyKads issued through the programme and did not represent the total number of new MyKads issued to the Orang Asli community in the state.
JPN was also obtaining identification data from the Department of Orang Asli Development (JAKOA) to determine how many Orang Asli in Kelantan did not have a MyKad or birth certificate as of 2026.
“The data will be used to help JPN review records and mobilise the MEKAR Programme, thereby ensuring that identified cases receive follow-up action and appropriate documentation assistance,” he said.
He said the total number of Orang Asli without the documents could not yet be confirmed as JPN had not received the data from JAKOA.
On another matter, Badrul Hisham said JPN had also identified issues involving permanent resident card (MyPR) or red MyKad holders, but the latest total was still being verified before it could be announced.
JPN stressed that each case had to be assessed based on the individual’s status and documentation to ensure the appropriate action was taken. — Bernama
